text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London reverted to their downward trend in late trading and closed at session lows. Benchmark October lost $1.50 to close at $323.20 per tonne, while December gave up $1.50 to close at $320.20 per tonne. The first beet test results from the Ukraine suggest that crop prospects are much better than last year. However, the area sown to sugar beet has been reduced by 24 per cent in effort to reduce surplus production which offsets the better beet test results.

Raw sugar futures in New York ended a volatile session lower. After some initial strength all of a sudden buying stopped and prices ended in the minus column. The October contract reached a high of 11.87 cents/lb before retreating to 11.59 cents/lb, 9 points lower than on Wednesday. March gave up 2 points to close at 11.78 cents/lb. Traders expect the market to test new highs due to improved fundamentals in 1997/98. On the other hand it should not be overlooked, that stocks are still fairly high and that at present at least there is no sign of a shortage developing.

DENMARK - The weather in the week ended August 3 continued to be good with local showers and a good deal of sunshine. Temperatures were above average. Precipitation levels since April 1 ranged between 177-247 mm compared to 198-209 mm in the long term mean. Growth is reported to be very good. Some regions report aphid attacks and other parasites while diseases still pose no threat. Production prospects continue to be normal.

AUSTRALIA ** - According to preliminary figures, sugar exports in June 1997, the first month of the 1997/98 campaign, amounted to 154,703 tonnes raws against 172,991 tonnes in June 1996. Total exports in 1996/97 amounted to 4.327 million tonnes compared to 4.177 million tonnes in 1995/96 and 4.479 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in June 1997 were Canada with 61,800 tonnes raws, down from 82,282 tonnes, Malaysia with 31,500 tonnes against 33,465 tonnes, South Korea with 21,570 tonnes compared to nil and Indonesia with 20,428 tonnes against nil.

UNITED KINGDOM - According to the first beet tests of August 4, the sugar crop in the United Kingdom is in very good shape with root weight at 440.8 grams, way above last year's 316.1 grams and also above the five year average of 387.8 grams. Sugar content is somewhat lower than last year (14.7 per cent vs 15.5 per cent) but the higher beet weight resulted in a sugar weight per root of 64.8 grams, more than 32 per cent up on last year's result. Given an almost unchanged area sown to beet the UK may expect to harvest a tonnage similar to the record seen in 1996 of 1.480 million tonnes, white value.

RUSSIA - Root weight in Russia on August 6 amounted to 204.8 grams, sharply up on the 178.2 grams of 1996 and also above the three year average of 197 grams. A sugar content of 10.4 per cent resulted in a sugar weight per root of 21.3 grams compared to 19.6 grams in 1996 and an average of 21.8 grams. Given the fact that the area sown to beet is down 12 per cent on the previous year the rise in sugar weight is unlikely to result in a higher overall production.

UKRAINE - The Ukraine is likely to have a rather good crop in 1997 given the last beet test results of August 6. Root yield per ha amounted to 14.6 tonnes compared to 11.2 tonnes in 1996, while sugar content was 10.3 per cent against 11.6 per cent. This resulted in a theoretical sugar weight of 1.5 tonnes, white value, per ha, up from 1.3 tonnes in 1996. The crop has still very good potential given a large number of beets per ha (82,000 vs 77,000 in 1996). However, the higher yields are unlikely to compensate fully for the drop in area which was above 20 per cent.

Syria's General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) has issued a buying tender for 13,000 tonnes of white sugar and 13,000 tonnes of raw sugar with September 9 set as final date to receive price offers. The two cargoes are for shipment in October. Results of the tender will be released on September 10. A GEZA tender issued on August 6 to buy 13,000 tonnes of white sugar for shipment between September 20 and October 20 is still valid, official sources said.
